recreation_prompt_markdown:
<!-- v5 recreation prompt -->

Create a portrait-first browser arcade game titled "Pellet Panic: Ghost Corridor". Preserve the source side-scrolling runner mechanics exactly: left/right horizontal movement, up jump, down crouch/fast-fall, gravity, auto-scrolling distance, accelerating speed, randomized obstacle/pickup spawning, AABB collision death, +100 pickups, start and restart overlays, and mobile on-screen controls. Reinterpret the presentation as a Pac-Man-inspired neon maze corridor: a yellow procedural chomper runs through glowing blue maze rails, ghost-shaped hazards occupy the old low/high/flying obstacle roles, pellets and power-pellet-styled dots occupy the old pickup role, and the HUD reads Pellets, Maze Run, and Pressure. Use Canvas, inline CSS/JS, Press Start 2P for arcade identity, large portrait controls, CRT scanlines, and mobile-safe overlays. Do not add lives, invulnerability, grid turning, ghost AI, or new scoring rules.
blueprint_markdown:
<!-- v5 source truth and protected blueprint -->

## Source Game Reality
- genre: single-screen browser canvas side-scrolling arcade runner
- objective: survive an accelerating route while collecting optional pickups for score
- input model: keyboard Arrow/WASD/Space plus mobile on-screen directional pads; left/right move horizontally, up jumps, down crouches/fast-falls
- core loop: start run, auto-scroll camera, spawn hazards and pickups, dodge hazards through jump/duck/positioning, collect items for +100, distance increases continuously, collision ends run, restart repeats
- fail/friction state: axis-aligned collision with any obstacle triggers game over; no lives or win condition

## Protected Mechanics
- Auto-scrolling distance, speed multiplier escalation, gravity/jump/crouch movement, rectangular collision, pickup +100 scoring, start/game-over/restart flow, keyboard and touch input semantics are preserved.

## Safe Theming Surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title, actor/hazard/reward names, canvas drawing style, background motifs, particles, feedback copy, fonts, palette, audio labels, and mobile chrome are safe to transform.
